items.titleEn: Apple stock rises as new macbook launch draws analyst support
items.summaryEn: Buy AAPL. The new MacBook Pro/iMac cycle plus higher price points supports revenue even while PC/tablet demand is weak. The M6/M5 Pro-Max push (faster on-device AI) strengthens Apple’s Services monetization path via paid “Apple Intelligence” features, not just hardware upgrades. Key risk: foldable iPhone display failures spread beyond “small number of units,” forcing costly redesigns/returns and hurting the premium brand narrative. Key Risk: Foldable iPhone screen cracking becomes widespread and forces expensive fixes and demand damage. Buy AAPL for the Services re-rating. If analysts are right that server-side Apple Intelligence features (including Siri) move to paid tiers, the market will treat Apple more like a recurring-revenue software platform, lifting the valuation multiple. The touchscreen OLED MacBook Pro also increases the installed base for AI workloads, accelerating Services adoption. Key risk: Apple delays or abandons paid AI/Services rollout, keeping AI monetization stuck in free tiers.

items.titleEn: GOOG stock plunges 13%: analysts cut PTs but remain bullish, betting on cloud growth
items.summaryEn: Buy Alphabet (GOOGL). The selloff is driven by near-term search monetization fears, but analysts still expect cloud to accelerate (Cloud >100% growth cited) and believe search headwinds are “navigable.” The stock’s worst post-earnings reaction since 2004 plus negative free cash flow is a classic setup for mean reversion if management shows improving AI Mode monetization and ad conversion. Key catalyst is investors re-rating toward cloud-led growth while treating search deceleration as temporary. Key Risk: Search monetization keeps deteriorating as AI Mode expands, forcing sustained margin/FCF damage and breaking the “temporary headwind” view. Sell Alphabet (GOOG) relative to Microsoft (MSFT) and Amazon (AMZN). The article flags a direct threat to Alphabet’s core ad engine from AI/agentic shopping and lower monetization per AI Mode query. While MSFT and AMZN also face AI disruption, their monetization is more diversified across cloud/software/commerce, so Alphabet’s earnings power is more fragile to search behavior changes. Use this as a relative-value bet that the market is over-penalizing Alphabet’s ad risk versus peers’ AI upside.

items.titleEn: Coherent stock may benefit from a Lumentum buyout, but there's a catch
items.summaryEn: Buy Coherent (COHR). Marvell weighing a Lumentum deal is a direct read-through: if Lumentum pays up, the market will re-rate COHR as the “cheaper, vertically integrated” laser/optics alternative (COHR forward P/E ~25 vs Lumentum ~40). COHR also has demand visibility (Lumentum products sold out through 2029) and strong recent growth/margins, so fundamentals can support the rerating even if the chart is ugly. Key Risk: Marvell never bids for Lumentum (or the deal collapses), removing the catalyst and letting the death-cross selloff dominate. Sell Coherent (COHR) short into the death-cross setup. If the 50-day EMA crosses below the 200-day EMA, momentum funds typically accelerate selling and price can slide toward $200 regardless of the AI narrative. Use this as a pure technical/positioning trade while the M&A story stays unconfirmed.

items.titleEn: Amazon earnings: can AWS growth satisfy Wall Street as capex rises
items.summaryEn: Buy Amazon (AMZN). Thesis: AWS revenue growth (~37% YoY to ~$45B) plus stable/expanding operating margin (~37% expected) can absorb rising depreciation from AI capex, keeping AWS as the cash engine while retail/ads cool. Rising capex is already priced, so the stock should re-rate if management shows AI infrastructure spending is translating into higher-margin cloud services (not just higher costs). Key Risk: AWS margins compress faster than revenue growth because AI infrastructure costs don’t convert into profitable demand. Sell Nvidia (NVDA). Thesis: the article flags hyperscaler capex exploding ($762B in 2026, $1.3T in 2027) but also warns near-term free-cash-flow pressure and uncertainty around AI service profitability. If hyperscalers delay or slow AI monetization, GPU demand can decelerate even while spending rises, hitting NVDA’s near-term earnings power.

items.titleEn: ServiceNow stock is plunging amid SaaSpocalypse fears: is this an overreaction?
items.summaryEn: Buy NOW. The report beat on revenue (+20.5%), raised full-year guidance, and lifted RPO (+22%) plus AI ACV to $1.7B. The drop is driven more by “SaaSpocalypse” fear than fundamentals, and the stock is now cheaper (forward P/E 38 vs 5-year avg 56). Expect a relief bounce as analysts digest the raised guidance and investors re-rate the growth durability. Key level: target ~$138 (June swing high). Key Risk: AI/automation fears prove justified—customers slow platform expansion or RPO growth decelerates sharply below guidance for multiple quarters. Sell NOW downside via a put spread (e.g., buy a lower-strike put and sell a higher-strike put) into the post-earnings panic. The thesis is mean reversion: modestly strong results + raised guidance should compress implied volatility after the initial overreaction, even if the stock chops lower briefly.

items.titleEn: Eli Lilly's blowout quarter has a $5.5 billion twist
items.summaryEn: Buy Eli Lilly (LLY). The quarter shows volumes up 53% and gross margin improving, while management raised full-year sales guidance by $5.5B—proof that cheaper access is still translating into profitable growth. The trimmed earnings outlook is largely acquisition-related charges, not demand collapse. Key risk: Mounjaro/Zepbound lose momentum (competition, coverage cuts, or reimbursement changes) fast enough that volume growth can’t offset lower realized prices. Key Risk: Mounjaro/Zepbound demand weakens due to competition or reimbursement/coverage changes, so volume growth can’t offset lower prices. Sell Novo Nordisk (NVO). If Lilly keeps converting lower prices into higher prescriptions (as shown by the volume surge and margin improvement), it gains share in obesity—directly pressuring NVO’s growth narrative. The market will reward the winner in GLP-1/dual agonist access expansion, and Lilly’s guidance raise is a clear relative signal. Key risk: NVO’s own obesity pipeline and pricing/coverage strategy accelerates, restoring prescription growth and narrowing the gap.
